title: Outbound stall — timestamped trace & hypotheses
content:
Quick scratchpad: intermittent outbound stalls seen from customer-23 private deployment after recent peering change. Symptoms: some TCP connections (mostly TLS) hang for 15-30s then succeed or fail with timeout, observed across a few nodes in cluster-a and cluster-b. DNS sometimes returns SERVFAIL during incidents. This file is chronological traces, commands I ran, partial outputs and borderline hypotheses — messy by design.

High-level symptoms observed:
- App-level requests to external APIs (payments, s3-like storage) hang intermittently; retries often succeed after 20-30s.
- curl --location to api.payment.example: TLS handshake stalls ~20s on some attempts.
- dig sometimes returns SERVFAIL for third-party resolvers during event window, but local dnsmasq usually ok.
- tcpdump shows repeated SYN retransmits from internal node to remote IP followed by RST/ACK from local gateway in some traces.

Timeline (local times, EST):
2024-11-05 09:12 - First pager: one tenant reported spike in 5xx and timeouts.
2024-11-05 09:18 - Confirmed across 3 hosts in cluster-a.
2024-11-05 09:22 - Ran quick tcpdump, saw SYN retries to 18.205.93.2 and rare ICMP unreachable from peering router.
2024-11-05 09:45 - Rolled back a recent BGP flapping rule (temporary), didn't change behavior.
2024-11-06 14:03 - Noticed correlation with large DNS cache churn on dnsmasq: loads of NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL to upstream.
2024-11-08 11:30 - Isolated to peered path: traffic to region-west third-party endpoints had higher error-rate than region-east.

Commands tried (snippets):
- tcpdump (short):
  sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 18.205.93.2 and tcp
  09:20:13.123456 IP 10.10.4.21.46012 > 18.205.93.2.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
  09:20:13.223567 IP 10.10.4.21.46012 > 18.205.93.2.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
  09:20:33.223999 IP 10.10.4.21.46012 > 18.205.93.2.443: Flags [S], ack 0, seq 12345, win 64240, length 0
  <-- retransmits, then a RST from our gateway sometimes seen.

- curl reproducer (from app pod):
  curl -v --connect-timeout 10 https://api.payment.example/charge
  * Connected to api.payment.example (18.205.93.2) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS 1.2 connection using ...
  * TLS handshake timed out
  * Connection #0 to host api.payment.example left intact

- openssl s_client (hang case):
  openssl s_client -connect 18.205.93.2:443 -tls1_2 -msg
  CONNECTED(00000003)
  random stuff... then nothing for ~20s, then: 
  ---
  no peer certificate
  ---

- dig / resolv checks:
  dig +short @127.0.0.1 api.payment.example
  ; sometimes returns IP, sometimes empty; repeated queries show SERVFAIL burst.

- system checks: ip route, iptables, conntrack counts
  ip route show default via 10.10.0.1 dev eth0 proto static
  sudo conntrack -L | wc -l => ~56000 (normal for this host at peak)
  sudo iptables -S | head -n 40 => no DROP rules for egress stack.

- BGP/peering: quick show (edge router team) reported intermittent prefix suppression around same times. Edge team says they saw flaps between our ASN and partner-isp for a 10-30s window.

Packet-level notes:
- Retransmits suggest packets leaving pod but no SYN+ACK from remote; could be blackhole or asymmetric routing.
- When RST observed, it's often from our gateway IP (10.10.0.1), which hints at some NAT/conntrack behavior or egress proxy interfering.
- TLS handshake stalls could be due to middlebox inspecting TLS (SNI rewrite) causing delay, or simply path MTU/fragmentation with middlebox dropping fragments.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Peering flaps causing transient blackholes/asymmetric routing -> SYNs lost, our stack retransmits, then gateway tears down flow. (Edge team logs support this)
2) DNS upstream intermittent SERVFAIL -> app retries pick different IPs which sometimes route to flaky path/ISP causing stalls.
3) Conntrack exhaustion or aggressive timeout on gateway -> gateway RSTs long-lived flows after seeing retransmits. (conntrack counts looked normal but need hist for per-port)
4) Middlebox (partner ISP) performing TLS inspection / rate-limiting -> handshake partial complete then hang. (less likely but seen historically)
5) MTU/fragmentation issue introduced by new peering path -> large TLS ClientHello fragmented and dropped.

Repro recipe (best-effort):
- From affected pod: while tcpdump running, curl -v https://api.payment.example/charge repeatedly in a loop (sleep 1) until you hit a hang.
- When hang seen, save pcap, note pod, node, timestamp. Try traceroute and tracepath to remote IP.

Quick traces that were captured (abbreviated):
- tracepath 18.205.93.2
  1: 10.10.1.1                                 0.330ms pmtu 1500
  2: 192.0.2.1                                 4.023ms
  3: 203.0.113.5                               12.342ms
  4: 18.205.93.2                               28.120ms
  (no hops shown as blackhole)

Open questions / things to check:
- Get full conntrack histogram for gateway during incident window.
- Any rate-limiting / DDoS mitigation on partner-isp side? Ask edge/contact.
- Confirm if any NAT44 translation changes were deployed prior to 11/05.
- Do we see similar behavior for non-TLS TCP (e.g., ports 80/8080) or UDP (DNS) to same IPs?
- Check MTU along peered path: enable iperf3 with MTU boundary testing (don't do on prod without consent).
- Capture full TLS handshake with Wireshark to see if FIN/ACK or TLS-level retransmits.

Notes-to-self:
- When saving pcaps, annotate with node/instance id + pod + container image.
- Keep an eye on dnsmasq logs: rotate to a dedicated file for incident so we can keep correlation.
- Push edge logs from 11/05 09:10-09:50 to S3 and ask edge team to correlate with partner-isp.

Immediate next steps (short):
- Ask edge team for BGP dump and prefix-suppression logs for 11/05 09:00-10:00. (Assigned to Liam)
- Pull conntrack stats (histograms) for gateway nodes for 11/05 and 11/06 windows. (Assigned to me)
- Add targeted tcpdump on gateway for flagged remote IPs with ring buffer. (Assigned to Ravi)
- Create reproducibility runbook: small script to loop curl+tcpdump and annotate PCAPs automatically.

Longer-term ideas:
- Add egress SLO monitoring per-customer/route (percentile latency + TLS handshake failure rate).
- Consider traffic shaping / alternate routing policy for peered routes when BGP churn detected.
- Harden DNS resiliency (fallback resolvers, increased cache TTL for some records).

References / links (duplicates of linked_artifacts above but inline):
- Jira: PEER-3412 (incident)
- Slack thread: #peering-hunt (C03F1J9KZ)
- Confluence: private-deploy egress playbook (draft)
- Local script: github.com/redwood/infra/peering-scripts#42 (pcap automation)

If anything else looks weird in the pcap I saved, paste here. For now, leaning toward peering-induced transient blackhole + DNS churn creating worst-case symptom surface.
